newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to end combined foreign cap on index futures.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to end combined foreign cap on index futures.

text.p: South Korea will remove the combined foreign investor trading limit in stock-index futures trade from July 7, when stock-index options are set to begin, the Securities Supervisory Board said on Friday.

The board said in a statement that it would remove the 30 percent limit on total foreign investor trading in index futures, but added that the individual foreign investor limit of five percent would remain.

Investors will be able to buy and sell products that expire within the next three consecutive months and three of the months of March, June, September and December, which are not included in the three consecutive months.
The market will have two types of options -- KOSPI 200 calls and KOSPI 200 puts.
The size of a contract was set at 100,000 won and trading hours will be 9:00-11:30 a.m. (0000-0230 GMT) and 1:00-3:15 p.m. (0400-0615 GMT) from Mondays to Fridays.
On the last trading day, the afternoon session will run from 1:00-2:50 p.m. (0400-0550 GMT), and Saturday's half-day session will run from 9:30-11:45 a.m. (0030-0245 GMT).
